missionPremise: P-124 CTX-B2 dispatch (2026-09-10): CADROLL_EXPECTATION_SQL compares dollar values across every historical cad_property row while the bake reads only the county's declared vintage, producing a false 22.1% miss rate on Hays; the fix must not ship without also confronting the A2 trap -- vintage-scoping alone would silently stop flagging 37,813 rows that were never genuine CAD accounts, which the bake's own recordRetirement mechanism may mislabel as 'left the roll'.

vintageGapVsNotFound_A2Trap.refinementThisLaneAdds_notPreviouslyRepo: CTX-SENTINEL's per-county family count is scoped to rows IN cad_property AT the declared vintage (Hays: 0). That answers 'does Hays' CURRENT roll contain non-account geometry rows' (no), not 'does an EXISTING BAKED SNAPSHOT for one of the 37,813 stale-vintage prop_ids carry (or would a future bake assign) a recordRetirement'. Those prop_ids are, by construction, absent from cad_property at every vintage except 2025, so buildRecordRetirement's declared-vintage-only check would retire them on any bake that reaches them -- a live-baked-snapshot question CTX-HAYS-SPLIT and CTX-SENTINEL did not measure, and this lane could not measure either without writing to or deeply auditing legacy-design-tools' live bake output, which is outside a postcondition-measurement lane's scope. lessons: LESSON: a worktree's checked-out branch is unrelated to which commit a git ref-level check (rev-parse, merge-base, log) reports -- /p/legacy-design-tools's own default checkout was on an unrelated stale branch (feat/s1-instrument-hardening) the entire session, which made a naive `find`/`grep` across its working tree return false negatives for files that exist perfectly well on origin/main. `git show <ref>:<path>` / `git grep <pattern> <ref>` read the object database directly and are immune to this; a working-tree-relative search is not.

LESSON: a module-graph or bundle tracer's own design principle ('bare specifiers are a bundle boundary') can be right in general and wrong in the specific case of an in-monorepo workspace package -- the distinguishing test is whether the specifier resolves to another directory IN THIS repo (repo content, esbuild bundles it) versus a published external npm dependency (a real boundary). Validate a tracer's completeness against the REAL bundler's own output (esbuild --metafile here) rather than trusting the tracer's own stated scope.

LESSON: before proposing any absence-state mechanism, grep _inbox/ for the exact phenomenon -- CTX-HAYS-SPLIT and CTX-SENTINEL had already measured and precisely reported the population this dispatch's A2 trap warns about, from two different angles, both awaiting the same operator ruling. Citing and refining beats re-deriving.

LESSON (for [[project_hauska_ctx_pipeline_architecture]]): a sibling lane's dispatch-cited branch name is not proof of that lane's progress -- always check the branch's OWN commit history (not just its existence) and separately check whether a live worktree with UNCOMMITTED local work exists, since both can be true, false, or a mix independently.
